$comment: ICU MessageFormat 1 -> canonical MF2 data model. Each test: `description`; `locale` (BCP 47, drives MF1 plural-key validation); `src` (MF1 source). A conversion case adds `mf2` (the expected message in MF2 syntax, for humans), `exp` (the expected canonical data model, shaped by ../unicode/data-model/message.schema.json and equal to `mf2` parsed) and `samples` ([{params, exp}]: `params` uses the Unicode suite's param shape, `exp` is the MF1 reference output, which the MF2 message must reproduce). A sample may carry `mf2Exp` (MF2 output, or null when the MF2 reference reports errors) for a known divergence explained by the case's `divergence`. An error case has `expErrors` ([{type}] with `mf1-syntax-error` or `mf1-unsupported`) instead. Mapping rules (Glossa decision, RFC 0002 §5): standard MF2 functions wherever they reproduce MF1 output; `mf1:`-namespaced functions with `mf1:argType`/`mf1:argStyle` attributes otherwise. Verified by gen/verify-mf1.mjs (see README.md); `exp` and sample outputs are derived with `npm run write`, everything else is authored.

tests.description: plain argument of a plural variable
tests.divergence: MF1 prints a plain {count} argument with String(value), so 2500 stays 2500. In MF2 the selector's .input {$count :number} applies to every {$count}, so it is locale-formatted (2.500). Values below 1000 without fractions format identically; the MF2 output is the correctly localized one.

tests.description: apostrophe-quoted hash inside a plural is text
duration keeps a non-standard mf1: function
date skeleton has no standard equivalent
tests.divergence: MF2 :date only knows fields/length, not ICU date skeletons. The argument keeps its MF1 type and style in mf1: attributes so it can be exported back to MF1 unchanged, but standard MF2 runtimes cannot reproduce it (the reference reports bad-option).

tests.description: number, currency without a currency code
tests.divergence: MF1 takes the currency from the formatter's configuration (USD by default); MF2 :currency requires the currency in the message or the operand. Kept as mf1:currency so the source round-trips; pass a currency-annotated value or rewrite the message with ::currency/XXX.
